what_it_does.name: better-auth-best-practices
what_it_does.summary: A single SKILL.md of instructions for setting up and configuring Better Auth, a TypeScript authentication library, in a project. It covers installing better-auth, setting BETTER_AUTH_SECRET and BETTER_AUTH_URL, creating auth.ts and a route handler and running migrations, with a quick reference for database adapters, sessions, plugins, hooks, security options and the client. It looks up documentation for the installed Better Auth version through the Better Auth MCP or better-auth.com/llms.txt. Use it when users mention Better Auth, betterauth or auth.ts, or need TypeScript authentication with email/password, OAuth or plugins.
tasks: install Better Auth and set its environment variables
create auth.ts and a route handler for the framework
run schema migrations with the built-in adapter, Drizzle or Prisma
configure sessions, cookie cache and secondary storage
configure security options, rate limiting and hooks
look up documentation that matches the installed version
what_it_does.author_description: Configure Better Auth server and client, set up database adapters, manage sessions, add plugins, and handle environment variables. risks.risk: A changed or compromised release of the auth CLI runs with the agent's privileges, since npx auth@latest fetches and runs the latest version unpinned.
Setting disableCSRFCheck or disableOriginCheck in advanced removes CSRF or origin protection from the auth endpoints.
risks.mitigation: both options are marked as a security risk

risks.risk: The auth secret ends up in source control when it is set as secret in auth.ts, which the config allows when BETTER_AUTH_SECRET is not set.
risks.mitigation: env vars are named as the first place for the secret, as guidance only

limitations: APIs and plugin names can differ across maintained release lines, so documentation must match the installed version.
Custom session fields are not cached in the cookie cache and are always re-fetched.
In stateless mode with no database the session lives only in the cookie, and the user is logged out when the cache expires.
Email verification works only when emailVerification.sendVerificationEmail is defined.
With secondaryStorage defined, sessions go there and not to the database by default.

known_problems.workaround: use the ORM model name in the config, not the database table name

known_problems.workaround: re-run the CLI after adding or changing plugins
